summary: This seat had no elected senator going in. Sen. Markwayne Mullin left the Senate, and the appointed interim senator, Alan Armstrong, did not run. Kevin Hern (Republican) won.

candidates.name: Kevin Hern
candidates.bio: Kevin Hern bought his first McDonald's restaurant in 1997 and has also worked in hog farming and banking. He has represented Oklahoma's 1st congressional district in the U.S. House since November 2018. He chaired the Republican Study Committee in the 118th Congress and the House Republican Policy Committee in the 119th.

positions.summary: Cosponsored a balanced budget amendment, which his campaign site presents as a way to address the national debt and curb spending.
Opposes extending the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, saying the underlying cost of health care is the real problem.
Voted for a bill to fund a border wall (H.R. 695) and cosponsored a bill to defund sanctuary campuses (H.R. 768).
Introduced the PROTECT Our Kids Act, which would bar Department of Education funding for any school that hosts a Confucius Classroom.
Cosponsored four bills (HR 369, HR 20, HR 616 and HR 962) that his campaign site describes as protecting human life and limiting abortion funding.

candidates.name: N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas
candidates.bio: N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas is a nurse, a Chickasaw citizen and an active-duty military spouse who grew up in Ardmore, Oklahoma. She won the Democratic nomination in the August 25 runoff.

positions.summary: Supports debt forgiveness and says she agrees with most of the Democratic Socialists of America platform, including free childcare and rent caps.
Says she wants to expand access to health care.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Vote totals read Nov. 25 from thegreenpapers.com. The State Election Board page at oklahoma.gov is headed OFFICIAL RESULTS, but it does not show the totals and the official count was not opened, so the race is not marked certified.
